translationRepairs: Wuhuang then sent Li Sixin and Li Cunshen to reinforce them, routed the Yan and Zhao armies, took thirty thousand heads, and captured their stores.
Wuhuang then sent Li Sixun and Li Cunshen to reinforce them, routed the Yan and Zhao armies, took thirty thousand heads, and captured their stores.
Chinese 李嗣勳 is Li Sixun (Sìxūn); idiomatic English wrongly renders it as Li Sixin.
In the fifth month Zhu Xuan of Yan was besieged by Bian and asked for help.
In the fifth month Zhu Xuan of Yanzhou was besieged by Bian and asked for help.
Chinese 鄆州 is Yanzhou; idiomatic English truncates it to Yan, which confuses with the Yan/Youzhou polity elsewhere in the chapter.
Wang Chongying of Hezhong had just died; his son Ke, Wuhuang's son-in-law, held command.
Wang Chongying of Hezhong had just died; Chongrong's son Ke, Wuhuang's son-in-law, held command.
Chinese 重榮之子珂 identifies Ke as Wang Chongrong's son, not Chongying's; idiomatic English wrongly makes Ke Chongying's son.
On gengshen Luo Quanzhen of the Palace Secretariat, seeing Wuhuang's army approach, urged the emperor to flee.
On gengshen Luo Quanguan of the Palace Secretariat, seeing Wuhuang's army approach, urged the emperor to flee.
Chinese 駱全瓘 is Luo Quanguan (瓘); idiomatic English wrongly uses Quanzhen.
That day they took Liyuan and two other forts, captured Zhijin, Lady Muqiu, Li Yuanfu, and two hundred more, and sent them to court.
That day they took Liyuan and two other forts, captured Xingyu's son Zhijin, Lady Muqiu, the general Li Yuanfu, and two hundred more, and sent them to court.
Chinese 行瑜之子知進 identifies Zhijin as Xingyu's son; idiomatic English omits the filiation.
In the second month Zhang Cunjing pressed Heyang; Wang Ke begged Wuhuang for aid, and envoys crowded the road.
In the second month Zhang Cunjing pressed Hezhong; Wang Ke begged Wuhuang for aid, and envoys crowded the road.
Chinese 河中 is Hezhong; idiomatic English wrongly says Heyang.
At the opening of the invasion Li Tang of Fen had rebelled and sided with Bian; Wuhuang now sent Li Sizhao and Li Cunzhen against him.
At the opening of the invasion Li Tang of Fen had rebelled and sided with Bian; Wuhuang now sent Li Sizhao and Li Cunshen against him.
Chinese 李存審 is Li Cunshen; idiomatic English wrongly renders it Li Cunzhen.
